Распределённый лок в Redis нужен в двух случаях.

(а) Бронирование разбито на несколько сервисов или шагов: "удержать место → подождать оплату → подтвердить". Держать транзакцию базы данных открытой всё время ожидания оплаты нельзя.

worst_places.before: **Database per Service** (a microservices practice) — each service owns its own database; nobody reaches into another service's DB directly. This gives isolation (a schema change in one service doesn't break others) and independent scaling, but creates a classic problem: a request needing data from multiple services requires **either** multiple requests merged at the API Gateway/BFF level, **or** a denormalized copy of the data (kept in sync via events) in the service that needs it.
worst_places.after:
**Database per Service** (a microservices practice) — each service owns its own database; nobody reaches into another service's database directly. This gives you isolation: a schema change in one service doesn't break the others. It also lets each service scale independently.

But it creates a classic problem: what about a request that needs data from several services? You have two options. Either send several requests and merge the results at the API Gateway / BFF (Backend For Frontend) layer. Or keep a denormalized copy of the data inside the service that needs it, kept in sync via events.

patterns: Abbreviations are expanded once per ZONE, not once per FILE — and the zone is read out of order. TTL is expanded only in article 03 but used in 02, 06, 07, 09, 11 and 12; CDN is expanded only in 02 but used in 01, in article 06's own title, and in 11 and 12; SPOF and NFR are expanded only in 01 but used in 10 and 11; DLQ only in 05 but used in 10; CQRS only in 04 but used as the framing of article 12's whole search section. This single habit accounts for most of the 151 mechanical abbreviation flags and for the A average of 3.0. The fix is one gloss-on-first-use pass per file, not new content.

Plain-text bracket cross-references that look like links and are not. The renderer (src/components/theory/ArticleRenderer.tsx) runs `marked` with no reference-link resolution, so `[Chat System]` reaches the phone as literal bracketed text. Article 11 has 9 in prose plus ~11 more inside ```txt blocks; article 12 has 12; articles 09 and 10 have 5-6 each. Worse, the bracket text does not match the article titles it points at (`[WebSockets]` vs the actual "WebSockets and Realtime Systems"; `[File Storage and CDN]` in the RU files vs the RU title "File Storage и CDN"), so even manual sidebar-hunting fails. Either make them real markdown links or drop the brackets and name the article in prose.

The `Senior-нюанс:` / `Senior nuance:` paragraph is used as a dumping ground: it typically carries the article's three or four hardest facts in one 35-50-word sentence with two nested parentheticals. It appears 20+ times across the zone and is where almost every over-length sentence lives (01 availability nines, 02 TLS termination and /health, 03 in-process cache, 05 exactly-once, 06 pre-signed URL security, 07 SSE, 11 time allocation). Keep the label — it is a useful signal of depth — but split the payload into 2-3 sentences.

Sections that open with a deferral instead of an answer. Article 02's first sentence is «Базовое различие ... разобрано в [System Design Fundamentals]»; article 11 §"Общая структура" opens «Эта последовательность была подробно описана в [...]»; article 11 §"SQL vs NoSQL" opens «Framework для выбора был подробно разобран в [Database Scaling]»; article 09's intro closes on the same move. A reader arriving from search is told where the content is not before receiving any content. Move the pointer to the end of the paragraph and lead with the fact — in every one of these cases the fact is already sitting in the same sentence's second half.

The EN locale is consistently harder than the RU it was written from, and not only because of the expected ~19% length inflation. Over-limit sentence rates roughly double (article 01: 12% RU → 27% EN; article 02: 20% → 43%), and F is 3 or below in all 12 files. Two causes: (a) RU sentences that were readable at 30 words become 45-word EN ones without being re-broken; (b) calques that produce non-English — "serve a multiple of the users" (03), "The practical consequence to fix here" (02), "Ordering — guarantees that cost something" (05) — plus idioms above B2 ("a bag of buzzwords", "close the door to a senior signal", "wide but shallow", "the same sin as", "reaching for a Redis lock"). The EN files need a sentence-splitting pass; the RU files mostly do not.

Wide two-column ASCII layouts inside ```txt blocks. Article 03's «Без кеша | С кешом», article 04's «До шардинга | После шардинга» and article 10's final-architecture diagram run 68-93 characters wide. The site renders these in a horizontally scrolling `<pre>`, so on a phone the second column is only reachable by side-scrolling — which destroys the side-by-side comparison the block exists to make. Every one of the 24 files has at least one line of 75-94 characters inside a fenced block.

Meta-references to the article's own revision history leak into the body text: «старая версия статьи правильно его обозначала» (ru/07:43, en/07:42 — in the opening sentence of that article's central section) and «(старая версия статьи)» / "(the old version of this article)" (ru/10:44, en/10:43). The reader has never seen an old version; these clauses are pure noise sitting in high-value positions.
notes: Four RU text-corruption typos where a non-Cyrillic character replaced a Cyrillic one: 低 for «низкую» (11:304), `bagажа` (11:342), `konце` (12:300), `ресharding` (04:100) — all four are byproducts of the zone-wide habit of declining Latin nouns with Cyrillic endings (`worker'ов`, `consumer'ами`, `bottleneck'ом`, 30+ instances). Also: ru/11:123 has a grammar error («Один и тот же функциональный требование»), and ru/12:362 has an English preposition in a Russian heading («Общие паттерны across всех 12 задач»). Register is inconsistent across the zone: articles 01-03 address the reader as «ты», article 11 uses «вы» 20 times. Every RU article title is untranslated English, which the rubric flags under G; I scored it as a zone-wide baseline rather than docking each file separately. Verdict is targeted-fixes rather than systemic-refactor because C/D/E average 3.7-3.8 — the concept sequencing, diagrams and code examples are genuinely strong and no article needs rewriting; the EN locale is the closest call, since its sentence-length problem is present in all 12 files.
